The curated store's advantage grows with overlap -- from parity where no key was shared, through +0.176 F1 where both keys were, to 25% fewer actions at +0.294 F1 on the trained questions, the one cell significant on both benchmarks -- while matching HippoRAG's gains with 1,913 links against its 196,112: per point of corpus covered, 1.5x the action saving and 2.1x the accuracy gain. Accuracy rises steadily with the share of the corpus the indexes cover, so training on more questions widens coverage, and with it the generalization.

title: DELE-w0.5: Inferring Action from Future Latent State for Robotic Manipulation
summary:
arXiv:2608.22067v3 Announce Type: replace-cross 
Abstract: World-Action Models (WAMs) build robot control on video-generation backbones, which jointly predict dense future visual trajectories and robot actions. We argue that video generation is an unnecessary intermediate objective for world-action modeling. For robotic manipulation, the goal of a world model is not to reproduce how the world looks at every intermediate moment, but to predict the state that the world will reach after an action is executed. The intermediate frames only describe the visual transition between physical states, which consumes substantial model capacity and computation, but do not directly specify the physical outcome that the robot action is intended to produce. In this paper, we propose DELE-w0.5, which infers robot actions from predicted future states without relying on video generation. Concretely, DELE-w0.5 infers the action sequence from its corresponding compact future latent state. The future latent state captures the action-relevant physical outcome of robot interaction and serves as an explicit bridge between world modeling and action generation. The core design principle of DELE-w0.5 is to model how the physical world changes under robot actions, rather than how its visual appearance evolves frame by frame. This formulation removes the high-dimensional visual redundancy introduced by dense video representations, and it therefore enables cheaper training and low-latency inference. Across 480 real-robot trials on four long-horizon manipulation tasks, our DELE-w0.5 achieves the best performance among all compared policies, attaining 62.5 overall full-task success and 81.3 macro ordered-stage progress, outperforming the strongest baseline by 47.5 and 30.7 percentage points, respectively.

title: SANE: State Anomaly Neutralization for Stable Extreme-Context Delta-Rule Models
summary:
arXiv:2608.22354v2 Announce Type: replace-cross 
Abstract: Delta-Rule recurrent models maintain a fixed-size state, enabling $O(1)$ inference memory but potentially becoming unstable under extreme-context extrapolation. By tracking RWKV-7 over sequences of up to 100M tokens, we empirically identify a distinct failure pattern: \textbf{localized norm explosion atop a relatively sparse substrate}, rather than global state saturation. Analysis of the recurrent update suggests that persistent decay keeps weakly updated entries small, whereas uneven injections allow a few channels to accumulate extreme values. Motivated by this diagnosis, we propose \textbf{State Anomaly Neutralization (SANE)}, which applies adaptive $\tanh$ compression at chunk boundaries while preserving the intra-chunk parallel structure. Within a safe threshold range ($3 \le \alpha \le 5$), SANE matches the baseline on 11 short-context reasoning benchmarks with no statistically significant degradation. After a 100M-token prefix, which exceeds the training length by over $24{,}000\times$, SANE retains functional reasoning ($33.46$--$35.56$) while the baseline encounters numerical overflow. In contrast, overly permissive thresholds ($\alpha \ge 8$) remain numerically stable but lose reasoning capability entirely, showing that numerical stabilization alone does not guarantee functional reasoning and revealing a capacity--stability trade-off in state compression.

title: Functional compatibility as a determinant of persistent neural learning
summary:
arXiv:2608.22462v2 Announce Type: replace-cross 
Abstract: Neural networks can acquire new capabilities while damaging existing ones, but what determines whether new learning persists remains unclear. We identify functional compatibility, the extent to which incoming learning can coexist with behaviour that must be preserved, as an experimentally manipulable causal determinant of persistence. From identical neural states, we vary compatibility while matching unrestricted learning opportunity and imposing a common retention requirement. Persistent learning increases with compatibility across independent directions, convolutional and transformer architectures, vision and text, and a ten-seed replication. Learning rules and retention constraints determine how much compatible opportunity is retained, whereas nonlinear geometry limits the matched intervention at larger update norms. Functional compatibility therefore reframes stability-plasticity from preventing forgetting to determining which new learning can coexist with existing function and persist.

title: The Mask Is Not the Model: Auditing Prefix Invariance in Attention, State-Space, and Hybrid Sequence Models
summary:
arXiv:2608.22876v2 Announce Type: replace-cross 
Abstract: Hybrid sequence models must satisfy prefix invariance: representations at position t must not depend on future inputs, yet this is rarely verified.
  We formalize prefix invariance and give a lightweight audit, two forward passes, no training or gradients, yielding a per-layer score localizing where causality breaks.
  Attention-mask inspection, the field's default check, is incomplete: causality is a graph-level property, and leaks can occur via scans, aggregations, or normalization despite correct masks. Across 192 injected-fault trials on eight checkpoints, mask inspection detected none, while our audit localized all 192/192 to the exact layer.
  Static/dynamic analysis of chunked-scan code in transformers found the same defect in Zamba2 and Nemotron-H, an inter-chunk axis error fixed via the reference implementation.
  The method fits on one page and runs in seconds.

title: Molecular LLM Agents: From Architectural Design to Scientific Autonomy
summary:
arXiv:2608.23104v2 Announce Type: replace-cross 
Abstract: Molecular science represents an important frontier for LLM-based agents. Unlike general agents that mainly operate over natural language, code, or web environments, molecular LLM agents must perceive, reason about, and act upon chemical objects across symbolic strings, molecular graphs, 3D conformations, spectra, simulations, and wet-lab measurements. Their capabilities depend on chemically faithful molecular perception, an LLM-centered agent framework, domain-specific tool grounding, and computational or experimental feedback, in addition to planning and tool use. This work develops a conceptual framework for molecular LLM agents from two complementary perspectives. First, we introduce an architectural view of molecular-agent design, covering molecular representation and perception, the agent framework, domain-specific toolboxes, and learning and optimization. Second, we propose a scientific autonomy ladder inspired by staged autonomy in engineering systems, categorizing agents into four levels: L1 assistive or fixed workflows, L2 adaptive computational agents, L3 feedback-aware physical experiment agents, and L4 scientific-agenda agents. Together, these two perspectives establish a comprehensive framework for comparing existing molecular LLM agents, identifying missing capabilities and deployment risks, and guiding the design, evaluation, and deployment of future agents in molecular discovery workflows.

title: How Much Regularization Survives Averaging? Update Masking in Federated Learning
summary:
arXiv:2608.23286v2 Announce Type: replace-cross 
Abstract: Federated learning on non-IID data seeks flat minima to generalize across clients, and existing methods borrow sharpness-aware minimization from centralized training. There is a second way to reach flat minima, in which the regularization comes for free from noise added to the parameter updates, and it has never been carried over to the federated setting as an implicit regularizer. We show the reason. Masking charges the optimizer for moving in sharp directions. We prove that when each client draws its own mask, federated averaging weakens that charge by exactly the cohort size, and that giving every client the same mask brings it back by a factor equal to the inverse gradient diversity of the cohort. In our experiment setting on CIFAR-10, that factor is 1.19 out of a possible 10. Turning off minibatch sampling raises it to 8.96, while changing data heterogeneity a thousandfold leaves it between 1.17 and 1.50. The configurations keeping the regularization train far too poorly to use.

title: Thinking Beyond Videos: Unifying Video Reasoning and Deep Research for Open-World Video Agents
summary:
arXiv:2608.23329v2 Announce Type: replace-cross 
Abstract: Open-world video understanding often requires a model to locate sparse visual evidence and acquire external knowledge that is absent from the video and its parametric memory. While Thinking-with-Videos enables active temporal perception and Deep Research supports multi-step information seeking, the two capabilities are typically developed in isolation. We introduce VideoRover, a unified Video Deep Research framework that iteratively coordinates video cropping, multimodal search, and webpage browsing. Given a video-question pair, VideoRover uses each tool result to select the next action, so localized video clips guide external retrieval and retrieved evidence triggers further video inspection and verification. To develop this capability, we construct an automated data curation pipeline, producing 26K verified SFT trajectories and 3K challenging RL instances. We also introduce VideoRover-Bench, a benchmark stratified by video duration and research difficulty. Experiments on VideoDR and VideoRover-Bench show that our VideoRover-8B-RL achieves performance comparable to proprietary models in the direct-answer setting without tool use while outperforming larger open-source models equipped with the same tool suite. Ablation studies and training dynamics further validate the complementary roles of active video grounding, external retrieval, and long-horizon reinforcement learning.

title: Cross-Domain, Multi-Task Data-to-Text Generation without In-Domain Training Data
summary:
arXiv:2608.23391v2 Announce Type: replace-cross 
Abstract: Structured data exists in many forms (tables, knowledge graphs, charts, and time series), and converting it into text may involve different generation tasks. However, most prior work on data-to-text (D2T) generation has focused on specific tasks and datasets, relying either on task-specific training data or on the zero-shot capabilities of large language models. We study cross-domain D2T generation in a setting where neither in-domain training text nor test references are available, and where domains, generation goals, and input structures vary substantially. We compare data-driven knowledge distillation (DDKD) against zero-shot inference and fine-tuning on out-of-domain D2T data, and introduce structure-preserving augmentation via structural subsampling and perturbation. Experiments on five benchmarks show that, at constant model size (1.7B parameters), DDKD consistently outperforms both fine-tuning and zero-shot inference. Moreover, the resulting small models outperform a much larger finetuned model on two of the five domains, achieving comparable performance on the remaining three. We further construct QUINTD-5, a fivefold extension of QUINTD-1, and show that simply scaling real target-domain inputs yields only modest gains, whereas our augmentation strategy remains more effective and more cost-efficient for cross-domain distillation.

title: What's the Catch? Evaluating Temporal Consistency in Vision-Language Models
summary:
arXiv:2608.23474v2 Announce Type: replace-cross 
Abstract: Vision-language models (VLMs) achieve strong performance on video and image-sequence benchmarks, yet it remains unclear whether they capture temporal structure. To study this question, we formulate temporal grounding as an anomaly detection problem, providing a simple and controlled evaluation that directly tests sensitivity to temporal consistency. We introduce TimeCatch, where temporal anomalies are created by swapping consecutive frames and frame-level anomalies by replacing a frame with Gaussian noise. Models are evaluated on anomaly detection and localization tasks across four synthetic and real-world datasets, alongside a human study. Our evaluation reveals a substantial gap between frame-level and temporal anomaly detection. While VLMs consistently detect frame-level anomalies and often localize them accurately, they perform near chance on temporal anomaly detection and only modestly above chance on localization. Humans, in contrast, achieve near-ceiling performance on both tasks. Additional analyses across model scales, prompting strategies, sequence lengths, and visual similarity suggest that these failures cannot be explained solely by limitations in perception or model capacity. Together, these findings indicate that current VLMs can identify anomalies within individual frames but struggle to integrate information across frames to reason about temporal consistency. TimeCatch provides a controlled benchmark for evaluating temporal grounding in vision-language models.

title: Best Practice Critic Optimization
summary:
arXiv:2608.23566v2 Announce Type: replace-cross 
Abstract: Group-based reinforcement learning methods such as GRPO for large language models avoid training a critic by sampling multiple responses for each prompt. A reliable critic could instead estimate token-level advantages from one response, but standard critic-based training recipes are often unstable. We study this instability and develop **Best Practice Critic Optimization (BPCO)**, a recipe that combines DPPO, value predictions bounded to the reward range, Monte Carlo value targets, unnormalized policy advantages, and length-adaptive generalized advantage estimation. Because the critic is used only during training, BPCO can also condition it on reward-defining information, such as a reference answer or grading rubric, that is hidden from the policy. Controlled experiments isolate the effect of each design choice. Across mathematical reasoning tasks with models ranging from 1.5B parameters to 30B-A3B mixtures of experts, BPCO improves a strong critic-based baseline consistently, and matches or exceeds a group-based baseline while sampling one response per prompt. The same recipe also improves learning with rubric-based rewards. These results show that a carefully designed critic provides a reliable alternative to group-relative advantage estimation. Code is available at https://github.com/QPHutu/golden_critic.

title: [Apple] mac-studio M5 Max36G+512G 丐版没有什么性价比啊，一直是可以预定的状态
[生活] 如何评价当今国际局势下，加入部分公司/行业意味着此生难以踏足北美大陆？

先说明，不是理性的分析，也不是建政贴，纯感性。
题主学生时代去过几次 us ，文化制度等等感觉也就是图个新鲜，但是北美一些独特的自然风光还是很令人喜欢的，比如西海岸常年二十来度的气温，和傍晚漫步在带一点沙地气候的海滩，都很惬意。东部波士顿🦐虽然俗，但是配着干净的大西洋海风，吃起来确实舒服。中部大平原还没去过，只从各种影视资料来看，也是我喜欢的那类，很期待有钱有闲了，去自驾横贯一回。往北一点，大瀑布，寒带，总之都很有意思。

哦，北美还有个墨西哥，emmm ，也能去看看吧，说整个北美洲好像有点过分了 hhh 。

title: [分享创造] 收藏了一堆做饭视频却从没真正做过？我们做了「一键大厨」
summary:
大家好，我们最近上架了「一键大厨」。
产品的起点是一个很日常的问题：在抖音、小红书刷到很多看起来不错的做饭视频，顺手收藏以后，却很少真的照着做。
并不是不想做，而是视频并不适合直接在厨房里执行：
食材和用量散落在字幕、口播和评论区里；
真正开始做时，要不断拖动进度条找步骤；
双手沾水、沾油以后，不方便频繁触碰手机；
收藏的视频越来越多，想做的时候却很难再找到；
看完一道菜，还要自己整理菜单和买菜清单。
我们想解决的不是“再提供一个菜谱库”，而是把已经收藏的做饭视频，真正变成可以执行的菜谱。
一键大厨目前可以做什么
把做饭视频整理成菜谱
粘贴做饭视频链接，或者上传本地视频，AI 会自动整理出：
所需食材和用量；
清晰的制作步骤；
对应的视频时间点；
可以保存和反复查看的图文菜谱。
以后想做的时候，不需要重新翻收藏夹、看完整段视频或者来回拉进度条。
建立自己的私人菜谱库
生成后的菜谱会保存到个人菜谱库中。
它更像是把散落在不同平台里的“做饭灵感”，整理成一个真正属于自己的菜谱收藏夹，而不是再让用户从一个公共菜谱库里重新搜索。

安排一周菜单，自动整理买菜清单
菜谱可以加入每周饮食计划，再根据安排整理购物清单。
从“这个看起来不错”，到“这周准备做什么、需要买什么”，可以在一个流程里完成。

做饭时按步骤跟做
进入跟做模式后，可以在图文步骤和原视频之间切换。
手上有水或者油、不方便碰手机时，还可以使用隔空手势切换上一步和下一步，尽量减少做饭过程中反复解锁和触碰屏幕。
我们现在还处在第一版
产品目前并不完美。
不同视频的拍摄方式、字幕、口音和剪辑节奏差别很大，AI 整理出的食材和步骤也可能出现遗漏或者理解不准确。我们正在重点优化：
哪些类型的视频最容易解析失败；
食材用量是否足够准确；
生成的步骤能不能真正照着做；
等待解析的过程是否清晰；
手势跟做在真实厨房里是否好用。


所以这次来 V2EX ，不只是想做一次产品介绍，也希望找到愿意实际导入一个视频、做一道菜并告诉我们哪里不好用的朋友。
V 友赠送一个月会员
下载安装并注册后，在 App 的「我的」页面找到用户 ID ，然后在评论区回复你的用户 ID ，我们会为对应账号赠送一个月 Pro 会员。
请只回复 App 内的用户 ID ，不要留下手机号或其他个人信息。
如果愿意，也欢迎顺便告诉我们：
你导入的是什么类型的视频；
生成结果是否准确；
哪一步让你觉得麻烦；
你更需要视频转菜谱、每周计划，还是跟做模式。
官网及下载：
https://chef.wyld.cc/
App Store：
https://apps.apple.com/cn/app/id6748383363
感谢大家体验。无论是建议、吐槽，还是解析失败的视频，都非常欢迎直接回复。对我们来说，现阶段发现问题比听到“挺好用”更有帮助。

title: [推广] 同样的模型，不一样的账单
summary:
RSI AI 是一个 API 网关。你的请求被转发到 Opus5 、Fable5 、GPT 5.6 的官方端点，价格是官方定价的 5%–15%。
一句没人愿意先说的话。
每个用前沿模型做东西的团队，月底都会经历同一个场面：有人打开账单页面，屏幕安静了几秒，然后有人说「贵是贵，但这就是它的价格」。
不是的。这是它从某一个特定入口进去的价格。
模型是同一个模型，权重是同一份权重，输出和你直连官方拿到的完全一致——因为它本来就是直连官方拿到的，你的请求落在官方端点上。整条链路里唯一变化的东西，是账单上那个数字。
RSI AI 到底是什么
一个 base URL ，一个 key ，你现在正在用的那套请求格式。
改客户端配置里的一行，其余代码一行都不用动。同样的 SDK 、同样的请求结构、同样的流式行为、同样的 tool use 语义、同样的返回对象。你的应用完全不需要知道我们存在。
base_url = "https://api.openai.com/v1"
base_url = "[ENDPOINT — ]"
接入到此结束，没有第二步。
现在说说你为什么不信
你就应该不信。「前沿模型 token 打一折」这句话，是一整个灰产的标准话术：把你的 Opus 请求悄悄换成便宜的开源模型、偷偷记你的 prompt 、转卖你的 key ，等到大规模退款来了就人间蒸发。如果你读到这一段的第一反应是「这听着像骗子」，说明你的判断力是正常的。
所以，换我们站在你的位置上，我们会想看到什么，以及我们要求自己做到什么：
路由可验证。 请求发往官方端点，任意一次调用的返回元数据里都能看到模型身份——不是写在宣传页上让你信，是写在 payload 里让你查。
绝不静默替换。 你要 Opus5 ，拿到的就是 Opus5 。不是微调版，不是蒸馏版，不是换了个标签的「效果相当」的模型。模型不可用时你收到的是报错，不是降级。
我们宁愿丢掉一个去核实之后没注册的人，也不想赚一个压根没核实的人的钱。
模型	RSI AI
Opus5 - 95% off
Fable5 - 85% off
GPT5.6 - 93% off
每百万 token 。
这东西适合谁
模型开销已经悄悄爬进支出前三的团队。一直在省着调 opus 、该用好模型的活儿却伸手去拿弱模型的独立开发者。以及所有跑 eval 、跑 agent 、跑批处理的人——那些「因为太贵所以最有意思的那版方案一直没做」的场景。
如果前沿模型的价格一直在替你做架构决策，这个约束现在可以拿掉了。该用贵模型的地方，就用贵的。
这东西不适合谁
如果你需要签正式的企业协议、需要合同层面的 SLA 、或者采购流程要求你和厂商建立直接关系，那就走官方。这是真实的需求，我们不会假装它不重要。

[职场话题] 互联网工作 5 年有感
summary:
最近这份工作越发糟心，估计要大变动，发点牢骚。
刚入职时，一切还是欣欣向荣，虽然也有工单、OnCall 让人劳累，但每天都在做技术拓展，每天大家讨论的都是如何做更好的架构、更好地赚钱。具体细节就不赘述。
最近 AI 的焦虑让非常多中低层领导焦虑，我的领导尤其。“外宽内忌，多谋少断”，脱离一线太久但自认为还是专家，外行指导内行。最近几年研发没做过任何技术决策，所有命令来源于他，不切实际、一眼收益极低投入极大的架构变动都是由他直接下发。从一开始就劝说，得到的回复永远是“行政命令”、“只管做”。满嘴 AI ，但自己对 AI 根本就没多少了解。喜欢虚头巴脑的“管理理论”，却自己应承担的责任全部甩锅，不沾一丝。
我也因为“怠惰”一只没挪窝...
最终垃圾命令得到垃圾结果，我这个执行者反成了他的甩锅对象，一切是因为我能力不行，哈哈。
和自己同学聊天，发现行业内这类人巨多，尤其较早入行，顺着互联网东风成为基干的，在最近 AI 浪潮下动作变形。无法想象草包成这样的一群人却能把持一切资源，公司也没任何纠错机制。
虽然自己还很年轻，还没到 30 ，但已经产生了离开互联网的念头，不想再和这群虫豸打交道了...

title: [分享创造] 1 个月之后，我把 PetOS 从「AI 桌宠」重新定义成了「桌面伙伴」
summary:
之前在 V2EX 发过一次 PetOS ，当时给它的定义还是：
一个常驻桌面的 AI 宠物。
最近重新做了一遍产品，我发现这个定位其实不太准确。
PetOS 想做的不是一个会聊天的桌宠，而是一个真正生活在你桌面上的伙伴。
所以现在，我们把它重新定义成：
Desktop Companion ｜桌面伙伴
它不需要你打开一个聊天窗口。
平时就待在桌面上，自己走走、发呆、休息。
你摸它、点它、和它聊天，它会有不同的反应。
聊得久了，它会记住你们之间发生过的事情，也会慢慢形成属于自己的情绪和性格。
我更希望它有点像小时候的 QQ 宠物——
不是“使用一个软件”，而是电脑里一直住着一个小家伙。
现在 PetOS 能做什么？
🐾 真正常驻桌面
透明置顶，不需要打开窗口。
它会自己活动，也可以拖拽、触摸、互动。
🧠 每个伙伴都有自己的记忆
不同宠物拥有独立的记忆和情绪。
你和它相处的时间越久，它才越像“你的那只”。
💬 它也可以主动找你
不是每次都要你点击聊天。
在合适的时候，它会主动说话；工作的时候也可以让它安静下来。
⏰ 陪伴之外，也能帮你一点忙
目前加入了专注模式、番茄钟、提醒等功能。
比如你开始专注工作后，它会安静陪着你，而不是一直打扰你。
🎨 不局限于官方宠物
现在支持 Codex Pet 资源，也可以从 Petdex 获取社区制作的角色。
所以你可以养官方角色，也可以把自己喜欢的角色带到桌面上。
为什么还要做一个“桌宠”？
其实现在已经有很多 AI Agent 、AI 助手、AI 聊天工具了。
但我一直觉得：
AI 不一定非要出现在一个聊天框里。
它可以是一个存在于你电脑里的“小生命”。
你写代码的时候，它就在旁边。
你摸鱼的时候，它也在旁边。
你工作几个小时以后，它提醒你休息一下。
有时候你甚至不需要和它说什么。
它只是在那里。
我觉得这才是「桌面伙伴」真正有意思的地方。
PetOS 目前支持 Windows / macOS，可以免费下载安装。
mac 端内测中， 尚未配置开发者账号， 所以各位大佬在首次打开时需要前往系统 安全与隐私=》仍要打开， 后续版本的热更新，只需要再次拖拽新版本到应用即可， 不用再 点击 仍要打开
官网：
https://www.petos.one/
目前还是一个持续开发中的项目。
如果你也是桌宠、AI Agent 、Electron 或有趣的玩家，欢迎来试试。
也很想听听大家觉得：
如果你的电脑里真的住着一个伙伴，你希望它是什么样的？

title: [程序员] 讲下我自己申请软著和商标的经历
summary:
刚才看见有大佬说自己申请软著一直待受理，就讲下自己的经历。

自己申请软件著作权
我第一次申请软件著作权，好像也是几年前在某平台找人申请的，好像也是几百块吧？后面申请是在淘宝或者拼多多上找商家申请的，比起几年前便宜很多了。
去年我第一次自己申请软件著作权，是因为朋友开发了一个 AI 软件著作权材料的平台，他给我送积分，够我生成 10 来个软件著作权的材料了。想着反正免费的，我就用他平台生成的材料试了下，材料通过 AI 生成之后会有很多文件直接下载，这个是我们申请需要的。
由于软件著作权我是第一次自己折腾，中间有 2 次没搞明白让补正资料的，这 2 次分别是：
软件的版本号我写错了，在申请的时候标题里面好像是不能带版本号的，因为版本号在下面已经添加了，我在标题里面也带了版本号，所以第一次的补正，我只改下标题的版本号就行了。
第二次是我上传的资料错了，我在 AI 平台生成的材料，有 2 份源代码文件，一份是 200 多页，一份是前后 60 页，我一开始上传的完整版，也就是 200 多页这个，被退回来之后，我上传了 60 页的这份资料，然后没几天就通过了。

后面我问了下朋友，他说源代码资料这个有时候也是看运气，如果第一次上传的完整版不通过，就上传 60 页这个；如果第一次上传的 60 页不通过，就上传完整版的。
自己在官方申请软件著作权是免费的，没有任何收费。自己整理材料就行了。自己申请适合不急需，如果你急需还是找下他们专业搞这个的吧，因为我也不知道他们是怎么在几个工作日搞定的？（美术作品著作权这个我倒是知道为什么有人可以在几个工作日注册下来）
由于我是自己第一次申请，被退回 2 次，所以我申请总共用了 3 个月左右，如果没有 2 次退回，应该 1 个多月是可以下来的。
今年他们好像对于 AI 生成的材料审核好像比较严格了？

自己申请商标
我第一次注册商标大概是 9 年前左右找人注册的，当时注册一个收了我 1200 还是 1300 来着？以前不懂这玩意，全权都是给她负责的，在那之后中间隔了好几年都没有注册过商标了，然后再次注册就是在第三方平台，主要是某 3XX 平台这边，中途也在腾讯云申请过商标，不过现在腾讯云已经不提供了。
第三方代理平台，之前普遍都是 270 或者 300 ，商标官网费用就是 270 ，第三方也收这个价，是因为他们刚做这个业务，所以没有加价。我大部分商标都是在 3XX 申请的，后面都是 300 一个，我有经验了所以都是走的基础套餐，去年有一个我想申请的商标，在 3XX 审核没有通过，其实我自己也知道这个商标大概率是不会通过的，但我的意愿只是想试一次，看看商标官方到底会怎么处理，可是在平台初审都过不了，那我就无法知道了，所以我才到商标官网注册账号，自己申请试一下。
我多年前都想自己在官方申请的，但是以前官方是不提供支付宝微信支付的，所以也就没继续了，不知道是什么时候开始提供了在线支付。因为商标我申请过很多了，所以中途没啥意外，就是注册账号，填写资料提交申请，等待结果，当然最终是没有通过，不过我知道结果了，也就可以正常使用了。

一些小众词的商标申请有时候也是看运气，毕竟是人工审核的，比如我曾经有个商标第一年申请没有通过，第二年申请就给过了，当然第二次申请的小类我删了几个，但是这种情况也不知道每一次都可以的，主要看审核的工作人员，有时候就算你小类不同也不给过。如果你急需或者你就是想要，那可以走复审。

我注册商标的小经验：到官方查询要申请的名称、先根据所申请的分类查，然后根据全部分类查询，最后拆分词再查询一次，这样就能大概判断自己申请的通过率了。
有一个提示：有时候一个词，几年前可以申请通过，几年后可能就无法通过了，因为这个词可能成为了一个大众词汇，那么就无法申请了，这个我也经历过。
当然如果你不想自己折腾，那就还是找人帮忙注册吧，我是这么多年来自己折腾太多次了。
